payload.instruction: Put a frog in the toilet
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the image provide sufficient evidence to determine whether the requested frog-in-toilet edit was made?
node.criteria: Pass if the toilet bowl and its contents are sufficiently visible to assess whether a frog is inside; fail if the image clearly shows the bowl but no frog inside; unknown if visibility or image evidence is insufficient. This check supplies evidence only and does not independently establish completion.
node.binding: Use only visible image evidence about the toilet bowl and its contents; unrelated edits do not count as progress.

node_traces.evidence: The toilet bowl and its contents are clearly visible, and a frog is visibly inside the bowl in the edited image.

dependencies.evidence: A frog is clearly visible inside the toilet bowl in the edited image.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is malformed/truncated (“visibly (...)”) and omits the source-to-edit comparison, while its criterion treats a single visible frog in the bowl as complete. In the edited image, one frog is clearly inside the bowl, but additional frogs are on the toilet lid/tank area and on the floor; the source has no frogs. This is evidence of progress, but the traces only verify presence inside the bowl and do not assess whether the requested edit is fully fulfilled under the rubric. Make the binding and criterion explicitly evaluate the requested change against the source and distinguish partial progress from completion using the whole edited scene, without assuming that any frog in the bowl alone settles fulfillment. Preserve an unknown outcome when evidence is insufficient. The support checks are valid and queried, so this is not a transport or dependency failure; their repeated high-confidence agreement is not independent evidence that the aggregate label is correct.
